newsitem.title: USA: Physician shrs hurt on fear Sierra deal off.
newsitem.headline: Physician shrs hurt on fear Sierra deal off.

text.p: Physician Corp stock fell four to 5-1/8 on Friday on fears that the planned acquisition by Sierra Health Services Inc was in jeopardy, analysts said.
On Thursday, Physician said that it would take a charge for its workers' compensation insurance unit.
"People are speculating that the deal will be cancelled," said Eric Handler, an analyst at JW Charles Securities. "If the deal goes through, Sierra is going to buy it at a substantially lower price."

On Thursday, Physician Corp said that it will take a $60 million charge for its workers' compensation business, then on Friday changed that figure to $80 million. In November, the company took a $130 million charge related to the same subsidiary.
"They are writing off over $200 of this business," said Handler. "This may put the company in default with its bank debt." Physician Corp officials were not immediately available for comment.
On November 4, Physician Corp said it would merge with Sierra. Under terms, each Physician Corp share would be exchanged for 0.45 shares of Sierra Health.

Sierra, which closed at 28-7/8 the night before the deal was announced in November, dropped to 23-3/4 after the announcement, and shares have remained off ever since. Sierra rose 2-3/8 to 27-1/8 on Friday.

"It looks like (arbitrageurs) are covering their shorts," said Mike Elwood, a research associate at Volpe, Welty & Co. "The arbs were short Sierra. When the news hit, they were covering their positions."
